summary.text: Son of Megapenthes in the Proetid line at Argos and father of Anaxagoras — the king in whose family's third the maddened women were cured and the kingdom was divided among Melampus, Bias, and Anaxagoras.
Not to be confused with the eponymous Argus son of Zeus and Niobe, nor with other homonymous Argeus figures in the Peloponnesian genealogies.

story.text: Pausanias names him only in the genealogical chain that binds the native third of Argos to the house of Proetus: Anaxagoras, son of Argeus, son of Megapenthes, was reigning when the women went mad and Melampus demanded an equal share of the kingdom for himself and Bias.
